name: T3 / thyroid fat loss

lead: T3 is the active thyroid hormone, available by prescription as liothyronine for hypothyroidism. In bodybuilding and cutting circles it has been used off-label to raise metabolic rate and lose body fat for a leaner look.

T3 raises basal metabolic rate, affects protein synthesis and increases sensitivity to catecholamines such as adrenaline. The prescribing label states that in people with normal thyroid function, ordinary hormone-range doses are ineffective for weight reduction and that larger doses can cause serious toxicity. No published trial of T3 as a cosmetic fat-loss method was found.

paras: Use is described mainly in bodybuilding contexts during short cutting phases, alongside calorie restriction and training, and usually discussed as a prescription-only drug obtained through a clinician. Reported timelines are weeks.

Excess thyroid hormone can cause sweating, tremor, insomnia, arrhythmias and heart failure. The label warns of serious or life-threatening toxicity at larger doses, especially alongside sympathomimetic amines. It can also suppress the body's own thyroid function. It is prescription-only in the UK and Canada.

angle.text: Users take the thyroid hormone T3 off-label during cutting phases to raise metabolic rate and shed body fat for a leaner look. The drug is approved for hypothyroidism, and its label states that normal-range doses are ineffective for weight reduction in people with normal thyroid function.

lead: Liothyronine is a synthetic form of triiodothyronine (T3), the more active of the two main thyroid hormones. It was approved for medical use in 1956 and is used mainly for hypothyroidism and myxedema coma.[1]

In this entry, 'T3 thyroid fat loss' refers to the practice of taking thyroid hormone, without a thyroid disorder, in an attempt to speed fat loss during a cut. The prescribing information for liothyronine states that in people with normal thyroid function, normal-range doses are ineffective for weight reduction and that larger doses can be seriously toxic.[1]
No published trial of T3 as a looksmaxxing or cosmetic fat-loss method was found.

paras: Liothyronine is prescribed for hypothyroidism and myxedema coma, and may be considered where peripheral conversion of T4 to T3 is poor. It has also been used in thyroid cancer care and as an add-on to some antidepressants.[1]
Liothyronine increases basal metabolic rate, influences protein synthesis and increases sensitivity to catecholamines. It has a faster onset and shorter half-life than levothyroxine.[1]

The product's boxed warning says that doses within the normal daily hormone range are ineffective for weight reduction in euthyroid people, and that larger doses may produce serious or life-threatening toxicity, particularly when taken with sympathomimetic amines.[1] Use for obesity is not recommended.[1]

Side effects resemble hyperthyroidism and include sweating, nervousness, heat sensitivity and weight loss; less common effects include diarrhea, headache, insomnia, tremor, irritability and menstrual changes. Excess doses can cause arrhythmias and heart failure. It is contraindicated in thyrotoxicosis and uncorrected adrenal insufficiency.[1]
No studies found on T3 for cosmetic or looksmaxxing fat loss in people with normal thyroid function.
